Trans-Taiga Road
TRANS-TAIGA ROAD
Detailed Travel Guide
Driving the Trans-Taiga Road
Overview Map
Virtual Tour
The Trans-Taiga Road is a gravel road that runs 666 km east
from near the top end of the
James Bay Road
. It
was built to access the various dams and generating stations that extend upriver
along the La Grande River.
This is an
extremely remote
road, leading 666 km
east - almost to Labrador - with no settlements or towns aside from Hydro
Quebec's settlements for workers (not open to the public). At the far end you
will be 745 km from the nearest town! This is the farthest you can get from a
town on a road in North America! (Not counting the private Hydro Quebec towns
that are not open to the public). Along this road is also the
farthest north
point you
can travel on a road in eastern Canada.
The road from
Brisay
(km 582)
to
Caniapiscau
is rougher and a 4-wheel
drive vehicle is recommended by Hydro Quebec. The main reason for this is the
very coarse gravel used for this road - there's large rocks littering the road
surface. However, I have heard from people who have driven this road in ordinary
passenger cars and they say it is fine. You do have to keep your eyes open for
the larger rocks though.
You should definitely travel this road only in a reliable
vehicle with good tires. It is not an overly rough road; passenger vehicles can
drive it, but it is gravel. Vehicle breakdowns here can be very costly. Flat
tires can be a serious (and expensive) incident if your tires are damaged. You
could be looking at having tires flown in on a non-scheduled flight - there are
no convenient "tire stores" up here! Please read
Driving the Trans-Taiga Road
first.
Although there are no towns, there are a couple of outfitters
along the way that sell fuel and offer meals and lodging. Cell phones do not
work here.
Generally the scenery is fairly level, but this road is
definitely more interesting than the
James Bay Road
. For
most of the length it runs through taiga: spruce and jack pine forest, bogs,
rocks, and low hills. This is about all you'll see apart from birds and some
wildlife, the occasional cabin a short distance off the road, and Hydro Quebec
installations. I once saw a couple of wolves playing in the middle of this road.
This truly is a
*VERY*
remote road. Do not approach a trip along it lightly.
Please read
Driving the Trans-Taiga Road
before traveling this road.

44450575.article_summary: The Trans-Taiga Road是魁北克一条长666公里的碎石路，通往La Grande River上游的水坝和发电站，极为偏远，沿途没有城镇，只有水电站的工人定居点且不对外开放。这条路途非常遥远，距最近城镇745公里，是北美最远的无城镇公路。从Brisay到Caniapiscau路段崎岖，建议使用四轮驱动车辆。尽管手机无信号，但沿途有一些提供燃料、膳宿的经营点。风景主要是寒带森林、沼泽、岩石和低丘，偶有野生动物。出发前需做好充分准备，确保车辆可靠，最好打印详细旅行指南。

data.title: The uncertain future of coding careers and why I'm still hopeful
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了编程职业未来的不确定性，尤其是在人工智能（AI）快速发展的背景下，许多新入行的程序员感到焦虑，担心工作是否稳定。作者承认这种担忧，但同时表达了对未来的乐观态度。作者认为，AI不会取代人类的创造力和 ingenuity，而是会帮助处理繁重的任务，让人类专注于更高层次的创新和发明。

为了在新的环境中 thrive，作者提出了几点建议：首先，我们要善于提供高质量的上下文信息，因为AI的有效性取决于此；其次，我们要学会引导AI解决问题，而不仅仅是操作工具；最后，我们要保持自己的创造力和好奇心，避免过度依赖AI。

总的来说，作者认为编程职业的未来不是被机器取代，而是被机器放大。编程的门槛会降低，但解决问题的能力、批判性思维和人类 ingenuity 的需求将更加重要。选择编程作为职业并没有错，这个行业正在转型，而不是消亡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）对软件开发及相关职业的未来影响，以及其对工作机会、职业发展、生产力收益分配等方面的潜在影响。

不同观点：
• **观点一**（[cardanome]等）：AI可以解放开发者，使他们从重复性任务中解放出来，专注于更具创造性和挑战性的工作。这被视为加速人类潜力的机会，但也有人指出历史上的技术革命往往带来短期的广泛痛苦，且长期可能导致人与工作疏离。争议在于：AI带来的生产力提升是会普遍造福社会，还是会进一步扩大贫富差距。

• **观点二**（[3D30497420], [disambiguation]等）：当前的AI发展被大公司和富人控制，可能导致这些权力拥有者利用AI谋取私利，损害公众利益。讨论点在于AI带来的知识共享是否真正公平，以及这些技术进步是否最终会服务于少数富人，而不是普罗大众。

• **观点三**（[billy99k], [freedomben], [zkmon]等）：AI可能导致大量初级软件开发者失业，特别是那些从事重复性、低技能工作的人。一些人认为，只有高级开发者或具备特定业务知识的人能够从AI浪潮中受益，而大部分从事“脏活累活”的人将面临失业风险。争议在于AI是否会导致软件开发行业的两极分化。

• **观点四**（[pclowes], [simonw], [jbs789]等）：AI是一种工具，而非威胁。持这种观点的人认为AI会提高生产力，但不会取代所有开发者，尤其是那些能够解决复杂业务问题的人。AI的普及可能改变工作的性质，而非完全消灭工作机会。这里的讨论焦点在于AI是否会降低某些开发者的价值，以及哪些技能将变得更为重要。

• **观点五**（[asimpletune], [lordnacho]等）：有人提出软件工程师应组建工会以应对AI带来的挑战，并制定行业标准和认证。还有人认为编程本质上是一个“临时性职业”，随着AI的发展，编程技能可能变得不再稀缺，正如过去的读写能力一样。讨论点在于是否需要通过专业化标准和认证来提高行业门槛，以及未来的职业发展路径是否会更加依赖于领域知识而非单纯的技术能力。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：AI带来的生产力提升将如何分配？当前趋势下，是否只会让富人更富，而普通员工面临更大的失业风险？

• **实际案例**：一些开发者分享了使用AI工具（如Cursor）的经验，指出AI在处理复杂任务时可能导致效率低下或产生混乱代码，甚至让使用者感觉自己像“初级程序员”。

• **未来展望**：部分评论认为AI会使年轻一代的开发者处于更有利的位置，因为他们可以更快适应新技术，而年长的开发者可能需要不断学习和适应以避免被淘汰。

44450812.article_content:
The Uncertain Future of Coding Careers and Why I'm Still Hopeful
A friend of mine, bright, driven, and relatively new to programming, asked me a heavy question the other day. “Did I make a mistake? Did I choose the right career?”
The question hung in the air. It wasn’t born from a bad day or a frustrating bug. It came from a much deeper place of anxiety, one that I suspect many in our industry are feeling right now. They saw recent waves of layoffs, they read the headlines about Artificial Intelligence, and they felt the ground shifting under their feet. The promise of a stable, in-demand career in tech, which seemed like a sure thing just a few years ago, now felt fragile.
“I’m so early in my career,” they said, “I worry if I’ll even have a job in a few years. It’s hard to stay motivated.”
I had to be honest. I hear them. Loud and clear.
I’m no expert, and my perspective is limited to my own journey, roughly 28 years in the tech world, nearly 15 of those as a full time software developer. I’ve seen a few cycles of boom and bust, but I’ll admit, this moment feels different. When I first got access to GitHub Copilot a few years ago, I had my own panic. I’m in my 40s. Was I becoming a fossil? How could I keep up?
That initial fear, however, eventually gave way to something else, a fire. It was a rallying cry to push myself, to embrace my love for learning, and to continuously grow. It reinforced a mindset I’ve tried to cultivate over the years, to constantly work to make my current role obsolete, because in doing so, I’m constantly working my way into my next one.
This is the sober part of the conversation, the industry has pendulums. Companies hire like mad for whatever reason, and then they overcorrect with layoffs. It’s a stressful reality. Imposter syndrome, that nagging feeling of being a fraud, doesn’t go away. I still feel it. But over time, I’ve learned to reframe it. Instead of feeling overwhelmed by all the brilliant people around me, I now feel a sense of awe and a desire to learn from them. It’s fuel.
But what about the elephant in the room, AI? My friend’s biggest fear was that AI will simply do what’s expected of a more junior engineer, making their role disappear.
This is where my hope for the future comes in.
I don’t believe we’re heading for a world where artificial general intelligence (AGI) makes human ingenuity obsolete. Look closely at every major breakthrough, even those in AI-driven medicine. It’s still humans pointing the AI down the right paths. Human creativity is the spark.
What I see is a future where AI handles the grunt work, freeing us up to focus on the truly human part of creation: the next step, the novel idea, the new invention. If we don’t have to spend five years of our early careers doing repetitive tasks, that isn’t a threat, it’s a massive opportunity. It’s an acceleration of our potential.
This led me to a profound realization that now guides my work. We are all, collectively, building a giant, shared brain.
Every time you write a blog post, answer a question on a forum, or push a project to GitHub, you are contributing to this massive corpus of human knowledge. The next generation of AI models will ingest that information. Your solution, your idea, your unique way of explaining something, becomes part of the shared intelligence of our species. When someone else, somewhere else, asks a question that overlaps with something you shared, they’ll be able to build on your work.
We are not just leveling up ourselves when we write and share; we are leveling up all of humanity.
So, how do we thrive in this new world?
First, we must become masters of context. The effectiveness of AI hinges on the quality of the information we give it. I’ve started obsessively collecting my own context, transcripts, notes, ideas, with the goal of building a personal, searchable database that I can use to augment my own thinking and my interactions with AI.
Second, we must learn to be shepherds, not just button-pushers. For those of us who write code, this means getting exceptionally good at describing problems and guiding AI to generate solutions. For our colleagues in non-engineering roles, it means learning to see opportunities for automation and building the AI agents to handle them. We all need to adopt a mindset of invention.
Finally, we must guard against brain atrophy. We can’t let the tool do all the thinking. Use AI as an accelerator, a tireless research assistant, and a pair programmer, but never as a replacement for your own curiosity and ingenuity.
So, did my friend make a mistake choosing to be a programmer?
Absolutely not. The barrier to entry for creating things with software will get lower, but this doesn’t devalue the profession, it transforms it. The demand for people who can solve problems, think critically, and apply human ingenuity will be higher than ever.

data.title: Whole-genome ancestry of an Old Kingdom Egyptian
data.author: A_D_E_P_T
data.article_summary: 本文报道了对古埃及Old Kingdom时期的一位成年男性木乃伊的完整基因组测序结果。该个体出土于Nuwayrat，生活在大约2855–2570 cal. BCE，处于早期王朝与古王国时期之间。其基因组显示，大部分祖先来自北非新石器时代人群，约20%的基因可追溯至肥沃新月东部的美索不达米亚及周边地区，表明古埃及与近东地区存在人类迁移和基因交流。此前由于DNA保存问题，埃及早期王朝的基因研究受限。此研究表明，古埃及不仅与近东有物质和文化交流，还涉及到人口迁徙，为理解古埃及人群的遗传多样性提供了新视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：古埃及人的起源、迁徙及其与周边地区的关系，以及相关政治和学术争议

不同观点：
• [rietta] 认为文章中提到的古埃及人与安纳托利亚和黎凡特地区在新石器和青铜时代的遗传亲和性并不令人惊讶。依据包括当时埃及与这些地区存在交流和人口流动，书面资料和圣经叙事也支持这种迁徙现象。

• [eddythompson80] 指出两个问题：首先，古埃及相关的重要发现中缺乏埃及考古学家的参与；其次，关于古埃及人从美索不达米亚迁徙到埃及的结论可能在政治上敏感。埃及官方和学术界倾向于强调古埃及文明的独特性和独立性，任何与此相悖的研究结果可能会引发政治争议。

• [hbarka] 提出地理变化的可能性，认为5000年前西奈半岛的地理形态可能与现在不同，陆地连接更多，使得当时的人们可以更自由地在不同地区之间移动，从而解释遗传亲和性。

• [andsoitis] 纠正时间线，指出古埃及社会并非存在了数千年，而是在约公元前3150年随着上下埃及的统一才开始兴起。

• [KurSix] 提出保存偏差可能导致我们错过许多早期的基因组数据，暗示我们对古代人口的理解可能不完整。

• [PKop] 质疑文章对墓主社会阶层的推断，认为无法确定墓主是上层阶级还是外来劳工，并指出墓葬方式与社会阶层的关联可能不准确，强调识别古文化中的人口和社会结构需谨慎。

补充讨论：
• 政治因素对古埃及研究的影响：[eddythompson80] 提到埃及政府和学术界对古埃及文明独立性的强调，以及任何与此相悖的研究可能会引发的政治问题。
• 地理变化对人口流动的影响：[hbarka] 提出地理变化可能促进了古代不同地区间的自由迁徙。
• 考古和历史研究中的不确定性：[PKop] 强调在推断古代人口和社会结构时需谨慎，特别是对墓葬和社会阶层的关联性分析。

争议焦点：
• 古埃及人的起源和迁徙问题在学术和政治层面上的敏感性，尤其是在涉及外来影响和文明独立性时，可能引发争议。

44450304.article_content:
Whole-genome ancestry of an Old Kingdom Egyptian
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Anthropology
Archaeology
Evolutionary genetics
Population genetics
Abstract
Ancient Egyptian society flourished for millennia, reaching its peak during the Dynastic Period (approximately 3150–30
bce
). However, owing to poor DNA preservation, questions about regional interconnectivity over time have not been addressed because whole-genome sequencing has not yet been possible. Here we sequenced a 2× coverage whole genome from an adult male Egyptian excavated at Nuwayrat (Nuerat, نويرات). Radiocarbon dated to 2855–2570 cal.
bce
, he lived a few centuries after Egyptian unification, bridging the Early Dynastic and Old Kingdom periods. The body was interred in a ceramic pot within a rock-cut tomb
1
, potentially contributing to the DNA preservation. Most of his genome is best represented by North African Neolithic ancestry, among available sources at present. Yet approximately 20% of his genetic ancestry can be traced to genomes representing the eastern Fertile Crescent, including Mesopotamia and surrounding regions. This genetic affinity is similar to the ancestry appearing in Anatolia and the Levant during the Neolithic and Bronze Age
2
,
3
,
4
,
5
. Although more genomes are needed to fully understand the genomic diversity of early Egyptians, our results indicate that contacts between Egypt and the eastern Fertile Crescent were not limited to objects and imagery (such as domesticated animals and plants, as well as writing systems)
6
,
7
,
8
,
9
but also encompassed human migration.

Article
Open access

Reconstruction of hundreds of reference ancestral genomes across the eukaryotic kingdom
Article
Open access
16 January 2023
Main
For thousands of years, the Egyptian Dynastic civilization (approximately 3150–30
bce
) developed monumental architecture, sophisticated technology and relatively stable belief systems, becoming the longest-lasting civilization known. Following the political unification of the northern and southern regions of Egypt (Lower and Upper Egypt) at the end of the fourth millennium
bce
, the Old Kingdom (2686–2125
bce
) witnessed considerable advances, including the construction of the first step pyramid complex of King Djoser and the ‘Great Pyramid of Giza’ built by King Khufu. The population has been considered to be of local origin, with limited input from neighbouring regions
8
,
10
. Yet, more recent archaeological evidence shows that trade connections existed across the Fertile Crescent since at least the sixth millennium
bce
7
, if not earlier, with the advent of the Neolithic package (such as domesticated animals and plants)
6
,
7
. Cultural exchange continued to develop through the late fourth millennium
bce
with the growing Sumerian civilization of Mesopotamia
7
,
8
,
9
. This period overlaps with the appearance of additional innovations in Egypt (such as the pottery wheel)
11
and the earliest evidence of hieroglyphic writing in the form of ivory tags in Tomb U-j at Abydos, dated 3320–3150
bce
7
.
Our knowledge of ancient Egyptians has increased through decades of bioarchaeological analyses
12
,
13
,
14
,
15
, including dental morphological studies on their relatedness to other populations in North Africa and West Asia
16
,
17
,
18
. However, the lack of ancient genomes, particularly for the early periods of Egyptian Dynastic history, remains a barrier to our understanding of population continuity and gene flow in the region. Although individuals from ancient Egypt were subjected to the first effort to isolate ancient DNA
19
, direct genome sequencing has remained elusive because of the challenging regional DNA preservation conditions. So far, only three individuals from Abusir el-Meleq (Fig.
1a
) have yielded nuclear DNA, all post-dating the emergence of Dynastic Egypt by thousands of years (from 787 cal.
bce
to 23 cal.
ce
)
20
. Moreover, these are not complete genome sequences but are limited to approximately 90,000–400,000 target-enriched genotypes. Over the millennia spanning the Dynastic Period, Egypt witnessed several wide-ranging wars, occupation by foreign rulers and dramatic episodes of internal political collapse (First, Second and Third Intermediate periods)
21
. Together, these processes may have substantially altered or reshaped the overall genetic structure and ancestry of the Egyptian population. Here we present a whole-genome sequence of an ancient Egyptian individual (2.02× coverage; Supplementary Table
1
), recovered from a necropolis at Nuwayrat (نويرات, Nuerat; Fig.
1a
).
Fig. 1: Geographic location and date of the Nuwayrat individual in context.
a
, Geographic location of the Nuwayrat cemetery (red dot) and the previously sequenced Third Intermediate Period individuals from Abusir el-Me

data.title: Conversations with a hit man
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 《The Atavist Magazine》的一篇文章讲述了退休的FBI特工Myron Fuller与雇佣杀手Larry Thompson在路易斯安那州监狱会面的故事。Fuller前往探访Thompson，最初是为了讨论一桩困扰他多年的谋杀案——Maria Marshall被雇凶杀害的案件。Thompson因多次雇佣杀人而被判长期监禁，他在会面中表现得十分友好，甚至有些热情。会面中，他们不仅讨论了Marshall的案件，还提到了其他案件。Fuller希望通过这次对话，能解开自己心理上的某些心结，因为当年在路易斯安那州任职期间，他未能阻止这起谋杀，这成为他职业生涯中的一大遗憾。文章描绘了两人之间的复杂关系以及这次特殊会面的场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一篇关于雇佣杀手和犯罪调查的文章展开的讨论，涉及法律程序、故事真实性以及对文章内容的个人感受。

不同观点：
• crossroadsguy：对司法系统中通过认罪协议减轻刑罚的做法表示质疑，认为这种做法不公正，并质疑具体案例中的操作方式和法官的权力限制。
• keiferski：对文章中描述的犯罪和腐败故事感兴趣，将其与电视剧《True Detective》类比，关注故事的背景和氛围。
• Communitivity：回忆起文章中提到的系列故事，对其中一名角色可能的真实性表示怀疑，但也表达了一种浪漫化的希望。
• garaetjjte：对文章中提到的人物故事持怀疑态度，认为讲述者可能在编造故事，指出其讲述的内容与公开信息不符，质疑其可信度。
• RickJWagner：对文章的写作表示赞赏，简单地对分享者表示感谢，没有深入讨论内容。
• Neywiny：认为文章值得一读，但对文章与讨论平台的关联性表示不解，不太清楚文章在特定网站上的作用。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于crossroadsguy对司法系统中认罪协议的合法性和公正性的质疑，其他讨论者更多关注文章的故事性和个人感受。
- garaetjjte对文章中具体人物和事件的真实性提出质疑，并通过细节分析来支持其怀疑态度。
- 部分讨论者（如keiferski和Communitivity）对文章的背景故事和氛围表现出兴趣，带有一定的情感和回忆色彩。

Conversations
with
a Hit Man
A former FBI agent traveled to Louisiana to ask a hired killer about a murder that haunted him. Then they started talking about a different case altogether.
By David Howard
The
Atavist
Magazine, No. 164
David Howard is a journalist and the author of
Chasing Phil: The Adventures of Two Undercover Agents with the World’s Most Charming Con Man
. He previously worked as an editor for
Backpacker
,
Bicycling
,
Popular Mechanics
,
and
Prevention
.
Editor:
Jonah Ogles
Art Director:
Ed Johnson
Copy Editor:
Sean Cooper
Fact Checker:
Kyla Jones
Illustrator:
Björn Griesbach
Published in June 2025.
1
The killer is happy
to see us. That’s the first thing we notice when we spot Larry Thompson halfway across the visitation room of the David Wade Correctional Center. He rises from a chair and waves, his face unfurling into an avuncular grin. Our separate journeys to this prison in Homer, Louisiana—me from Maine, and Myron Fuller from the mountains of Utah—afforded plenty of time to set expectations, and neither of us anticipated a Norman Rockwell greeting. I pictured a menacing scene bathed in the neo-noir lighting of
The Silence of the Lambs.
And Fuller? He long believed that the next time he and Thompson saw each other would be through gun sights.
The visitation room Warden Jerry Goodwin escorted us into is large, square, and filled with cafeteria-style tables. It’s December 2021. Lights on a small artificial Christmas tree wink, at once cheery and monstrously sad. Vending machines line one wall, glowing sentinels filled with bags of junk food. During normal visiting hours, the chatter of reunited families animates the room. But Fuller is a retired FBI agent with an illustrious career, I’m an experienced journalist, and Thompson is a model inmate, his vast criminal history notwithstanding. As such, Goodwin has granted us special privileges: an open-ended block of time, and a dedicated room with no bars or glass partitions, just a bored-looking guard at a nearby desk.
“Larry,” Fuller says.
“Good to see you,” Thompson drawls. The two old adversaries take chairs facing each other across six feet of wood laminate. I perch on a bench halfway between them and fan out the objects I’ve been permitted: notepad, pen, digital recorder.
At 78, Thompson is 18 years into an 80-year prison sentence for attempted first-degree murder and aggravated burglary. (A 35-year federal term theoretically begins after that.) One morning in 2003, Larry and his son Larry Neal Thompson Jr., along with four other men, robbed an Intertrust Armored Services car. They were spotted by a witness—a rare event in Thompson’s long criminal career—and a cop chased their escape van. One of the men shot an AK-47 through the officer’s window, wounding him. A massive manhunt ensued, and after several hours all six of the perpetrators were caught. They were subsequently convicted. Then, in 2014, Thompson confessed to four murders for hire in exchange for a reduced prison term for his son. (That deal never went through, because the official who overseeing it died before it could be finalized.) Thompson was later transferred to Wade from the maximum-security Louisiana State Penitentiary—better known as Angola.
Seated before us, he wears the standard-issue uniform: blue jeans and a light-blue chambray shirt. His hangdog blue eyes are framed by gaffer-taped tortoiseshell glasses that rest atop his prominent nose. His hands are missing parts of two fingers. “This one I cut off with an electric drill,” he’ll tell us later, holding up the stump of his left index finger. Then he’ll wave the remains of his right ring finger. “My dog bit me on this one.”
The warden tells us goodbye, then turns to Thompson. “Behave yourself,” he says, not unpleasantly. Goodwin hesitates for a beat, as if he wants to say something to us or is curious about why we’re here. Cops come to interview prisoners all the time, of course, but he doesn’t see many 79-year-old retired FBI agents dropping in on one of his more notorious inmates.
Fuller shakes Goodwin’s hand and thanks him. The truth, as best Fuller can grasp it himself, is that he’s hoping to dislodge a few ghosts from his psyche. He enjoyed an illustrious 31-year career in the bureau, with one notable exception: his tenure running the office in Shreveport, Louisiana, from 1981 to 1985.
What went wrong? Only everything. Crooked cops. Investigations that inexplicably faceplanted. Political interference. Wiseguys and one particularly ethically challenged attorney. And, most prominently, a murder Fuller believes he could have prevented: Maria Marshall, a mother of three. It was a hired job; her husband, saddled with debt, wanted to collect the life insurance. The hit man was Larry Thompson.

data.title: Gmailtail – Command-line tool to monitor Gmail messages and output them as JSON
data.author: c4pt0r
data.article_summary:
**gmailtail** 是一个命令行工具，用于实时监控 Gmail 邮件并以 JSON 格式输出，便于自动化和集成。主要功能包括：

1. **实时监控**：持续监控新邮件。
2. **灵活过滤**：按发件人、主题、标签、附件等过滤。
3. **断点支持**：从上次停止的地方恢复监控。
4. **多种输出格式**：支持 JSON、JSON Lines 和紧凑格式。
5. **配置文件**：使用 YAML 文件进行复杂设置。
6. **Gmail 搜索语法**：支持 Gmail 强大的搜索查询。
7. **简易认证**：支持 OAuth2 和服务账户。

安装和使用步骤包括通过 `uv` 工具进行安装和配置，并提供了多种使用示例，如监控特定发件人、过滤未读邮件、以及使用 `jq` 进行高级操作。工具还支持自定义输出字段、断点管理和配置文件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于邮件处理工具和方法的技术讨论，以及对现代应用程序趋势的看法。

gmailtail
A command-line tool to monitor Gmail messages and output them as JSON, designed for automation, monitoring, and integration with other tools.
Features
🔄
Real-time monitoring
- Continuous monitoring of new emails with
--tail
mode
📧
Flexible filtering
- Filter by sender, subject, labels, attachments, and more
💾
Checkpoint support
- Resume monitoring from where you left off
🎯
Multiple output formats
- JSON, JSON Lines, and compact formats
⚙️
Configuration files
- YAML configuration for complex setups
🔍
Gmail search syntax
- Full support for Gmail's powerful search queries
🚀
Easy authentication
- Support for OAuth2 and service accounts
Quick Start
Install using uv (recommended):
#
Install uv if you haven't already
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh
|
sh
#
Clone and setup the project
git clone https://github.com/c4pt0r/gmailtail.git
cd
gmailtail
uv sync
Set up Google API credentials:
Go to
Google Cloud Console
Create a new project or select an existing one
Enable the Gmail API
Create credentials (OAuth 2.0 Client ID for desktop applications)
Download the credentials JSON file
Run gmailtail:
uv run gmailtail --credentials credentials.json --tail
Installation
Using uv (recommended)
#
Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/c4pt0r/gmailtail.git
cd
gmailtail
#
Install dependencies and create virtual environment
uv sync
#
Install in development mode
uv pip install -e
.
Usage Examples
Basic monitoring
#
Monitor all new emails
gmailtail --tail
#
Monitor emails from specific sender
gmailtail --from
"
noreply@github.com
"
--tail
#
Monitor with Gmail search query
gmailtail --query
"
subject:alert OR subject:error
"
--tail
Filtering options
#
Monitor unread emails only
gmailtail --unread-only --tail
#
Monitor emails with attachments
gmailtail --has-attachment --include-attachments --tail
#
Monitor specific labels
gmailtail --label important --label work --tail
#
Monitor since specific date
gmailtail --since
"
2025-01-01T00:00:00Z
"
--tail
Output formats
#
Pretty JSON output
gmailtail --format json --pretty --tail
#
JSON Lines format (one JSON per line)
gmailtail --format json-lines --tail
#
Compact format
gmailtail --format compact --tail
#
Include email body
gmailtail --include-body --max-body-length 500 --tail
#
Custom fields only
gmailtail --fields
"
id,subject,from,timestamp
"
--tail
Checkpoint management
#
Resume from last checkpoint
gmailtail --resume --tail
#
Reset checkpoint and start fresh
gmailtail --reset-checkpoint --tail
#
Custom checkpoint file
gmailtail --checkpoint-file ./my-checkpoint --tail
Configuration file
#
Use configuration file
gmailtail --config-file gmailtail.yaml
#
Example configuration file
cp gmailtail.yaml.example gmailtail.yaml
#
Edit gmailtail.yaml as needed
gmailtail --config-file gmailtail.yaml
Advanced usage with jq
#
Extract only sender email and subject
gmailtail --format json-lines --tail
|
jq -r
'
.from.email + ": " + .subject
'
#
Filter emails by specific sender and get only timestamps
gmailtail --format json-lines --tail
|
jq -r
'
select(.from.email == "noreply@github.com") | .timestamp
'
#
Count emails by sender
gmailtail --format json-lines --once
|
jq -r
'
.from.email
'
|
sort
|
uniq -c
|
sort -nr
#
Get all unique labels across emails
gmailtail --format json-lines --once
|
jq -r
'
.labels[]?
'
|
sort
|
uniq
#
Extract emails with attachments and show attachment info
gmailtail --format json-lines --include-attachments --tail
|
jq
'

#

.subject
'

osascript -e
"
display notification
\"
$subject

with title
\"
Urgent Email

"
;

#
Extract email body text and save to files
gmailtail --include-body --format json-lines --once
|
jq -r
'
"\(.id).txt|\(.body // .snippet)"
'
|
while
IFS=
'
|
'
read
filename content
;
do
echo
"
$content
"
>
"
$filename
"
;

Monitor GitHub notifications and extract PR/issue numbers
gmailtail --from
"
notifications@github.com
"
--format json-lines --tail

44450182.article_summary:
**gmailtail** 是一个命令行工具，用于实时监控 Gmail 邮件并以 JSON 格式输出，便于自动化和集成。主要功能包括：

1. **实时监控**：持续监控新邮件。
2. **灵活过滤**：按发件人、主题、标签、附件等过滤。
3. **断点支持**：从上次停止的地方恢复监控。
4. **多种输出格式**：支持 JSON、JSON Lines 和紧凑格式。
5. **配置文件**：使用 YAML 文件进行复杂设置。
6. **Gmail 搜索语法**：支持 Gmail 强大的搜索查询。
7. **简易认证**：支持 OAuth2 和服务账户。

安装和使用步骤包括通过 `uv` 工具进行安装和配置，并提供了多种使用示例，如监控特定发件人、过滤未读邮件、以及使用 `jq` 进行高级操作。工具还支持自定义输出字段、断点管理和配置文件。

data.title: Nightmares Linked to Faster Ageing and Premature Mortality
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 新研究发现，频繁的噩梦与生物学上的加速衰老以及过早死亡风险增加三倍有关。英国痴呆症研究所的Abidemi Otaiku博士分析了4196名26至74岁成人的数据，结果显示，每周做噩梦的人过早死亡风险显著增加。研究通过表观遗传时钟测量生物衰老速度，发现频繁噩梦者衰老速度更快。噩梦通过加速细胞衰老过程，解释了约39%的噩梦与过早死亡之间的关系。因此，频繁噩梦应被视为加速衰老和早死的可修改风险因素，临床实践中应筛查并治疗噩梦，以改善睡眠质量、心理健康，并可能降低死亡风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：梦境与 nightmare（噩梦）的成因、变化以及可能的干预方法

不同观点：
• **lqet** 分享了自己在有孩子之前经常做关于杀人 guilt（罪恶感）的噩梦，但在第一个孩子出生后噩梦就停止了。这暗示了生活阶段的变化（如成为父母）可能对梦境有影响。
  
• **jkmcf** 表示自己长达45年一直做噩梦，且不认为这与缺乏锻炼或衰老有直接关系，似乎认为噩梦是长期存在且不可解释的现象。

• **BLKNSLVR** 提到自己很少做梦或记住梦，并认为对噩梦的了解可能反而会让人做更多噩梦。同时，他指出对现实的接受态度可能影响梦境记忆，但不确定这两者是否相关。

• **3shv** 以幽默方式表示自己多数梦到的是死亡，认为这可能预示着自己的未来，暗示梦境可能与个人对命运的看法有关。

• **NoPicklez** 提出了饮食（特别是乳制品）可能导致 GI distress（胃肠不适），从而引发噩梦的观点，并引用了相关文章，提出食物不耐受可能影响梦境质量。

• **rapjr9** 分享了个人经历，提到服用 NAD+ 补充剂（Elysium Health's Basis）后梦境变得无趣，暗示补充剂可能有减少噩梦的效果，尽管只是 anecdotal evidence（个人经验）。

• **billy99k** 观察到戒掉咖啡因后，梦境记忆恢复且睡眠质量改善，暗示咖啡因可能对梦境和睡眠有影响。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：梦境的成因尚无定论，不同人对于梦境的变化有不同的解释，包括心理因素（如生活阶段变化、对现实的态度）、生理因素（如饮食、补充剂）等。

• **饮食与梦境的关系**：NoPicklez 和 billy99k 提到了饮食（乳制品、咖啡因）对梦境和睡眠的影响，这为梦境的生理成因提供了可能的解释。

• **干预方法**：rapjr9 提到 NAD+ 补充剂可能对减少噩梦有效，尽管这是基于个人经验，但提供了一种潜在的干预思路。

• **梦境与现实的关系**：部分评论（如 BLKNSLVR 和 3shv）提到了梦境与现实态度、命运预示等的关系，反映了梦境可能具有的心理暗示作用。

44449958.article_content:
FREQUENT nightmares are linked to accelerated biological ageing and a threefold increase in the risk of premature death, according to new research presented at EAN 2025  by Dr Abidemi Otaiku of the UK Dementia Research Institute.
Nightmares have long been associated with neurodegenerative diseases, but their broader impact on health and ageing has remained unclear. This study is the first to demonstrate that nightmares are not only distressing but may also be a significant, independent predictor of faster biological ageing and earlier mortality in the general population.
The study analysed data from 4,196 adults aged 26 to 74, drawn from four large population-based cohort studies, with a total follow-up of 18 years. Nightmare frequency was self-reported at baseline, and premature mortality was defined as death before age 75. The study used Cox regression to examine the association between nightmare frequency and premature death, while biological ageing rates were measured using a composite of three epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge, PhenoAge). During the follow-up period, 227 premature deaths occurred. Adults who reported weekly nightmares at baseline had a more than threefold increased risk of dying before 75 compared to those with no nightmares (adjusted hazard ratio 2.73; p<0.001). Furthermore, individuals with frequent nightmares exhibited significantly faster rates of biological ageing (p<0.001). Mediation analysis revealed that accelerated biological ageing explained approximately 39% of the relationship between nightmares and premature mortality, suggesting that the stress and sleep disruption caused by nightmares may directly impact cellular ageing processes.
These findings highlight the importance of recognising and addressing nightmares as a modifiable risk factor for accelerated ageing and early death. For clinical practice, this suggests that patients presenting with frequent nightmares should be screened for underlying sleep disorders, stress, and mental health issues, and offered appropriate interventions such as cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia or image rehearsal therapy. Given that nightmares are both common and treatable, targeted interventions could not only improve sleep quality and mental well-being but may also contribute to healthier ageing and reduced mortality risk. Further research is needed to confirm whether treating nightmares can slow biological ageing and extend lifespan, but the evidence already supports a proactive approach to nightmare management in routine healthcare.
Reference
Otaiku A. Nightmares accelerate biological aging and predict premature mortality in humans. Abstract OPR-111. EAN Congress, 21-24 June, 2025.

data.title: Super Simple "Hallucination Traps" to detect interview cheaters
data.author: EliotHerbst
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在工作及面试中的应用及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• [careful_ai] 认为AI工具应该融入工作流程，而不是打断或劫持流程。他指出，过度依赖AI工具可能导致工作流程的割裂，增加提示和上下文切换的负担，理想状态是增强工作效率而非造成分心。

• [Reubend] 对在面试中使用AI工具持怀疑态度，特别是当候选人被问及是否使用LLM（大型语言模型）时，可能会产生困惑和不解，认为这种做法不够透明。

• [MotiBanana] 分享了在DevOps领域使用AI工具的实际体验，发现AI在处理不存在的概念（如"Fluxion"）时会出现混淆，但也能尝试给出合理的替代解释，表明开发相关问题的复杂性。

• [nrds] 支持在面试中使用技术性问题，例如实现递归下降算法解析JSON文件，认为这是合理的面试问题，并不超出合理范围。

• [poulpy123] 以讽刺的口吻指出使用AI拒绝使用AI的人的矛盾现象，类似于一些大公司一面宣称AI的优越性一面禁止候选人在面试中使用AI。

• [derbOac] 对AI模型的虚构问题感到好奇，质疑为何模型会如此频繁地产生虚构信息。

• [leakycap] 质疑在面试中被AI工具欺骗的可能性，认为通过面对面或实时视频面试可以很快判断候选人的实际能力，而不应依赖过多的异步测试或书面作业。

• [Kemschumam] 提出使用图像或手写问题等方法来测试候选人是否依赖AI工具，以防止候选人在面试中作弊。

补充讨论：
• AI工具在工作中的最佳实践：如何平衡AI增强与分心。
• AI在面试中的应用：透明度、合理性及其实际效果。
• 面试官与候选人之间的互动与判断能力，特别是在技术面试中的角色。
• 防止候选人使用AI作弊的策略与方法。

争议焦点：
• AI工具在面试中的使用是否合理透明。

data.title: Astronomers discover 3I/ATLAS – Third interstellar object to visit Solar System
data.author: gammarator
data.article_summary: MPEC 2025-N12报告了ATLAS望远镜发现的一个新天体：3I/ATLAS = C/2025 N1 (ATLAS)。该天体在四张于7月1日拍摄的图像中被发现，拥有高度偏心、超双曲轨道（e ~ 6）。初步观察显示可能有彗星活动，伴随微弱彗发和3角秒长的尾迹。观测数据来自多位天文学家，进一步的观测被鼓励以精确确定其轨道和性质。所有观测数据可通过MPC Explorer实时获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕新发现的第三个星际物体（3I）的科学分析、可能性推测以及未来观测的讨论。

不同观点：
• **科学分析与数据解读**：
  - [ddahlen] 提供专业见解，解释该星际物体的轨道特性（偏心率超过6）、大小估计（8-22公里，取决于表面反照率），并提到如果该物体活跃（如彗星），其尘埃可能使其看起来比实际大。他还指出该物体逆行，并预测其在接近太阳时的行为。
  - [jerpint] 则表示对数据不了解，询问如何将这些数据解释为一个实际物体。

• **天文观测技术的进步与未来发现**：
  - [ordu] 提出两种假设：人类天文学家观测技术的提升，或宇宙中即将出现大量类似物体。
  - [zeristor] 认为新投入使用的Vera Rubin望远镜将发现更多此类物体。
  - [jcfrei] 期待更大口径的望远镜（如ELT）上线，认为会带来更多新发现。

• **星际物体数量与宇宙学意义**：
  - [martinclayton] 引用了学术论文中的数据，讨论星际物体的数量估计，并进行计算推测在土星轨道范围内可能存在一个这样的物体。
  - [isx726552] 提到小说中的情节与现实中发现的对比，认为现实中发现的星际物体数量增加迅速。

• **对星际物体异常性质的讨论**：
  - [rjinman] 认为发现更多类似彗星的星际物体，使Oumuamua（1I）显得更加怪异。

• **科幻与假设**：
  - [fouronnes3] 提出科幻性假设，认为前两个星际物体是外星飞船的废弃阶段，而3I是主船。
  - [m3kw9] 表达希望该物体是外星智慧生命来访，尽管这是一个不受欢迎的观点。

• **人类应对与技术能力**：
  - [artur_makly] 询问如果该物体直接朝地球而来，人类目前是否有能力阻止。
  - [renrutal] 则开玩笑提到是否能搭便车，并指出只有Project Orion可能追上其速度。

补充讨论：
• **具体信息查询**：
  - [belter] 提供了一个维基百科链接，指向有关3I的更多信息。

• **宇宙学与过滤理论**：
  - [carlsborg] 提到“大过滤器”理论，暗示星际探测需要跨越光年的距离，可能影响我们对星际物体的探测和理解。

争议焦点：
• **科学解释与科幻假设之间的冲突**：一部分讨论围绕科学数据的解释和科幻假设之间的矛盾，例如外星飞船的假设与实际观测数据的对比。

3I/ATLAS = C/2025 N1 (ATLAS)
A new NEOCP candidate A11pl3Z was discovered by ATLAS Chile (W68) in four
30-second survey images taken on July 1 UT. Immediate follow-up and precovery
observations by Q.-Z. Ye (I41) and S. Deen (W68, M22), including data from
June, revealed a highly eccentric, hyperbolic orbit (e ~ 6). There are
tentative reports of cometary activity from X09 (S. Deen), G37 (Q.-Z. Ye)
and T14 (R. Weryk) with a marginal coma and a short 3" tail at a position
angle 280 deg. Additional observations are strongly encouraged to better
constrain the object's orbit and nature. Any additional observations received
by the MPC will be officially published in the MPC's standard `Orbits and
Observations of Comets` publication.

data.title: Fei-Fei Li: Spatial intelligence is the next frontier in AI [video]
data.author: sandslash
data.article_summary: 本文列出了与YouTube平台相关的一些重要链接和信息。包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻、版权声明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者选项、使用条款、隐私政策、安全政策以及如何使用YouTube的指南。此外，还提到正在测试的新功能和NFL Sunday Ticket服务。文章末尾注明了版权归属为2025年的Google LLC。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（尤其是LLM）在空间推理和物理世界建模中的局限性，以及对未来发展的讨论。

不同观点：
• jandrewrogers认为，物理世界的建模问题远比Fei-Fei所描述的复杂，尤其是涉及非线性和稀疏系统的动态建模。他指出，LLM在处理空间动态方面存在根本性的不匹配，并质疑Fei-Fei团队中是否有人具备解决这些问题的专业知识。
• skwb指出，当前ML领域的就业市场过度关注LLM，导致计算机视觉领域受到冷落，尽管计算机视觉仍有重要研究产出。
• alganet质疑空间智能AI是否只是复杂的感知系统，而缺乏真正的智能。他以三叶虫为例，指出AI在基本决策能力上仍有缺失。
• weinzierl分享了使用LLM进行地理定位的体验，指出LLM在识别模式方面表现出色，但在处理空间关系时表现不佳。
• owenpalmer则持相对乐观态度，展示了LLM在生成3D场景文件方面的能力，认为LLM在空间智能方面仍有潜力。
• jgord强调了3D重建的重要性，并分享了自己在3D处理方面的进展。他认为通过现有的ML/RL方法可以大幅提升3D处理能力，而不需要AGI。
• IdealeZahlen讨论了空间推理的个体差异，指出空间推理可能与内部视觉化基础的推理不同。
• myspeed认为，人类的许多空间智能是天生的，通过进化发展而来，而AI在这方面的能力需要重新学习和适应。
• sabman分享了在卫星领域处理多维度图像数据的挑战，指出其独特的问题和解决方法。
• wolframhempel介绍了在物理空间操作优化方面的实践，展示了Fei-Fei理念的实际应用。
• czbond指出IEEE已批准的空间网络标准，并暗示Fei-Fei的理念并非全新。

补充讨论：
• District5524提到对Fei-Fei年龄的关注，认为这是不重要的题外话。
• moktonar提出了一个哲学性观点，认为智能不仅需要身体，还需要环境作为进化的基质，并建议通过量子计算模拟现实环境。
• Nurbek-F质疑Fei-Fei的理念是否与Karpathy早期对Tesla Vision的倡导相似。

争议焦点：
• jandrewrogers对Fei-Fei团队的专业知识和理解能力表示怀疑，认为他们可能低估了问题的复杂性。
• skwb和alganet对当前AI研究方向表示担忧，认为基本的空间和时间动态问题仍未解决。
• 对LLM在空间智能方面的潜力存在分歧，jandrewrogers和weinzierl的观点相对悲观，而owenpalmer则较为乐观。

总的来说，讨论围绕AI在空间推理和物理世界建模中的能力和局限性展开，涉及理论、技术和实际应用多个层面。

• myspeed认为，人类的许多空间智能是天生的，通过进化发展而来，而AI在这方面的能力需要重新学习和适应。
• sabman分享了在卫星领域处理多维度图像数据的挑战，指出其独特的问题和解决方法。
• wolframhempel介绍了在物理空间操作优化方面的实践，展示了Fei-Fei理念的实际应用。
• czbond指出IEEE已批准的空间网络标准，并暗示Fei-Fei的理念并非全新。

补充讨论：
• District5524提到对Fei-Fei年龄的关注，认为这是不重要的题外话。
• moktonar提出了一个哲学性观点，认为智能不仅需要身体，还需要环境作为进化的基质，并建议通过量子计算模拟现实环境。
• Nurbek-F质疑Fei-Fei的理念是否与Karpathy早期对Tesla Vision的倡导相似。

争议焦点：
• jandrewrogers对Fei-Fei团队的专业知识和理解能力表示怀疑，认为他们可能低估了问题的复杂性。
• skwb和alganet对当前AI研究方向表示担忧，认为基本的空间和时间动态问题仍未解决。
• 对LLM在空间智能方面的潜力存在分歧，jandrewrogers和weinzierl的观点相对悲观，而owenpalmer则较为乐观。

总的来说，讨论围绕AI在空间推理和物理世界建模中的能力和局限性展开，涉及理论、技术和实际应用多个层面。

data.title: You People Keep Contradicting Yourselves
data.author: taylorlunt
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一种常见的网络争论现象：人们常常因为个人的言论与某个群体（或普遍观点）不一致，而指责其为伪善。文章以Bhavye Khetan欺骗风投获取会议的推文为例，分析了某人被指责为伪善，仅仅因为他与某个群体（即便与他本人无关）的言论相矛盾。作者指出，这种"关联伪善"的指责反映了社会的部落化倾向，人们更倾向于将个体视为群体的代表，而不是独立的个体。这种互动模式可能是有毒的，因为它忽视了个体的独特观点和独立性。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• dataflow反驳danscan，认为他正在做自己所指责的行为，即错误地将言外之意归咎于他人。dataflow指出，Rob Bailey的评论并没有称任何人为伪君子，而是指出了一种常见的矛盾现象。dataflow还强调，人类自然会做出假设，这是正常的，解决方法是更合理地处理这些假设，并对他人观点抱有更多宽容。

• briangriffinfan询问如何有效地指出他人的错误，而不会引发对方的下意识否认和反击，并质疑这种现象是否表明了讨论的恶意。
• scrubs认为，社交媒体激励极端立场和象征性的争斗，因为这可以带来关注和流量。这种环境使得人们更倾向于攻击群体而非个体。

• DonsDiscountGas质疑文章中的某个例子是否足以说明“游戏被操纵”。
• lijok认为，这种现象是由于人们的懒惰和寻找最廉价的方式来验证自己的世界观。
• moralestapia指责xir做了同样的错误行为，并提出一种讽刺性的解决方案。
• weare138批评Rob guy使用了稻草人论证和诉诸权威的经典诡辩技巧。
• subjectsigma表示，曾经试图分析这类问题，但后来意识到这种努力无助于改变现状，因此停止这样做。

- 争议的焦点在于人们是否在在线讨论中容易做出错误的假设和泛化，以及如何有效地解决这种现象。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是社交媒体环境如何影响对话质量，特别是其对部落主义和极端立场的激励作用。
- 自我反省和同理心在在线讨论中的重要性也被多次提及，szszrk和dataflow都强调了理解和宽容的必要性。

44451313.article_content:
←
See all posts
You People Keep Contradicting Yourselves!
’politics’
’rationality’
I saw this tweet
1
recently:
A tweet by Bhavye Khetan in which he brags about tricking VCs into having mettings with him after he lied to them about his credentials
The guy lied to get meetings with VCs. As far as I can tell, this is the system operating exactly how it should, and I have really nothing to say about that. What I want to talk about is this popular response:
A response to Bhavye Khetan’s tweet by Rob Bailey, calling Bhavye Khetan a hypocrite.
Specifically, point #1. "People complain VCs don't take cold inbound. So don't complain if they try to."
Do you see the problem? Rob Bailey is calling Bhavye Khetan a hypocrite because Bhavye Khetan said something that contradicts something that "people" say. But "people" and Bhavye Khetan are not the same thing?
I'm not trying to pick on this Rob Bailey guy — it's a common pattern I've noticed online. People will argue with an individual as if that individual is the spokesperson for a larger group. People will call someone a hypocrite not for contradicting
themselves
, but for contradicting
other people
.
"Oh, you think sex work should be decriminalized? I was under the impression you feminists thought sex work was exploitative?"
Why should an individual feminist be beholden to what every other feminist has said? Maybe some feminists think sex work is exploitative and some don't. Yet too often people accuse others of
hypocrisy by association
. I bet now that I've pointed it out, you'll start seeing it everywhere.
2
If you say something that contradicts what a group you're loosely associated with has said (even if that group is just "people in general"), then you must be a hypocrite.
But why does this happen? Have we grown so tribalistic that our default mode of interaction is now team vs. team rather than person vs. person? Can we no longer recognize that individuals may have their own opinions that differ from those of their tribe? If so, that sounds pretty toxic. But maybe it's comforting to believe you're combatting an ideology, rather than a mess of millions of individuals who all have different lives and believe different things.
Footnotes
Actually, I saw
Anthony Sistilli's video about the tweet
↩
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency_illusion

data.title: CEOs Start Saying the Quiet Part Out Loud: AI Will Wipe Out Jobs
data.author: planetjones
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）对行业、就业市场的影响以及企业CEO对AI的看法和利用。

不同观点：
• **对CEO利用AI进行炒作和裁员的批评**：[asielen]认为，大多数CEO对AI的理解有限，他们只是利用AI作为借口进行大规模裁员，以提升股价并在短期内获利。这种做法被视为不负责任，且CEO们并不真正关心AI的实际能力或其长期影响。
• **具体时间框架的讨论**：[BLKNSLVR]指出，很多关于AI导致失业的预测缺乏具体时间框架。虽然像Elon Musk这样的企业家在做大胆声明时承担风险，但其他CEO的声明则显得更为模糊和不可验证。
• **AI对就业市场的直接影响**：[jmathai]认为，AI本身不会取代工作，但那些善于使用AI的同事会取代不使用AI的人。这种观点强调了掌握AI技能的重要性。
• **人类决策的角色**：[jamesgill]强调，AI并不是自主做出雇佣或裁员决策的主体，背后仍然是人类在资本主义竞争中做出的选择。因此，AI的影响并非不可避免，而是人类决策的结果。
• **对未来劳动力成本减少的怀疑**：[xkcd-sucks]对企业基于尚未发生的劳动力成本减少进行炒作表示怀疑，认为这些预期应持保留态度。
• **对裁员策略的支持与批评**：[CjHuber]和[mensetmanusman]对某些裁员策略提出批评，暗示这些策略可能会导致不良后果。而[bravetraveler]则支持通过裁减海外廉价承包商并雇佣本地员工来提高利润。

补充讨论：
• **AI实施的技术挑战与就业机会**：[dworks]认为，每个AI应用案例都需要特定的工作流程和大量的工程师来实现，因此广泛采用LLM（大语言模型）可能会导致就业机会增加，而非减少。
• **对AI炒作文章的怀疑**：[sandspar]怀疑一些文章可能是为了点击率而制造恐慌，并指出其周围的人在面对AI影响时采取了不同的生活方式，如提前退休或尝试新业务。
• **长期观察与反思**：[derbOac]提到，一些CEO喜欢戏剧性地夸大AI的影响以吸引注意力，但这种做法可能会在未来导致 regret。同时，更现实和谨慎的观点也存在。

争议焦点：
• **CEO对AI的声明是否可信和负责任**：一方认为CEO们在利用AI进行炒作和短期获利，另一方则认为这些声明可能包含具体时间框架和实际风险。
• **AI对就业市场的长期影响**：一方认为AI会导致大规模失业，另一方则认为AI会创造新的就业机会，关键在于人类如何适应和利用这项技术。

data.title: Bridging Shopify and Shipstation on Heroku: A Story of Custom Fulfillment
data.author: kevinhq
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在特定情况下（如Shopify与ShipStation的数据交付问题），请求缓存和系统重启的处理方式。

不同观点：
• 观点一：[lucfranken] 提出问题，询问在Shopify已交付但无法交付到ShipStation的情况下，系统是否会缓存所有请求，以及当服务重启时会发生什么。这暗示了对数据丢失和请求处理的担忧。
   
• 观点二：隐含的观点是系统可能没有缓存机制，或者缓存机制不够健全，导致在服务重启时可能会丢失请求或出现交付失败的情况。这反映了对于系统健壮性和数据一致性的关注。

补充讨论：
• 请求缓存的必要性：[lucfranken] 的提问表明了对系统在异常情况下（如交付失败或系统重启）如何确保请求数据不丢失的关注。
• 系统重启的影响：讨论涉及系统重启可能导致的请求丢失问题，这是系统可靠性和数据完整性的一个重要方面。
• 具体场景的关注：特别提到了Shopify和ShipStation这两个平台，表明了在实际应用场景中（如电商订单处理）可能遇到的实际问题。

争议焦点：
• 系统在处理交付失败和重启时的缓存机制是否足够健壮，能否确保数据不丢失。这直接关系到系统的可靠性和用户体验。

总结：讨论围绕系统在交付失败和服务重启情况下的请求缓存和数据完整性问题，关注缓存机制的必要性和有效性。

44450513.article_content:
A little while back I heard about the White House launching their version of a
Drudge Report
style website called
White House Wire
. According to
Axios
, a White House official said the site’s purpose was to serve as “a place for supporters of the president’s agenda to get the real news all in one place”.
So a link blog, if you will.
As a self-professed connoisseur of websites and link blogs, this got me thinking: “I wonder what kind of links they’re considering as ‘real news’ and what they’re linking to?”
So I decided to do quick analysis using
Quadratic
, a programmable spreadsheet where you can write code and return values to a 2d interface of rows and columns.
I wrote some JavaScript to:
Fetch the HTML page at
whitehouse.gov/wire
Parse it with cheerio
Select all the external links on the page
Return a list of links and their headline text
In a few minutes I had a quick analysis of what kind of links were on the page:
This immediately sparked
my curiosity to know more about the meta information around the links
, like:
If you grouped all the links together, which sites get linked to the most?
What kind of interesting data could you pull from the headlines they’re writing, like the most frequently used words?
What if you did this analysis, but with snapshots of the website over time (rather than just the current moment)?
So I got to building.
Quadratic today doesn’t yet have the ability for your spreadsheet to run in the background on a schedule and append data. So I had to look elsewhere for a little extra functionality.
My mind went to
val.town
which lets you write little scripts that can 1) run on a schedule (cron), 2) store information (blobs), and 3) retrieve stored information via their API.
After a quick read of their docs, I figured out how to write a little script that’ll run once a day, scrape the site, and save the resulting HTML page in their key/value storage.
From there, I was back to Quadratic writing code to talk to val.town’s API and retrieve my HTML, parse it, and turn it into good, structured data. There were some things I had to do, like:
Fine-tune how I select all the editorial links on the page from the source HTML (I didn’t want, for example, to include external links to the White House’s social pages which appear on every page). This required a little finessing, but I eventually got a collection of links that corresponded to what I was seeing on the page.
Parse the links and pull out the
top-level domains
so I could group links by domain occurrence.
Create charts and graphs to visualize the structured data I had created.
Selfish plug: Quadratic made this all super easy, as I could program in JavaScript and use third-party tools like
tldts
to do the analysis, all while visualizing my output on a 2d grid in real-time which made for a super fast feedback loop!
Once I got all that done, I just had to sit back and wait for the HTML snapshots to begin accumulating!
It’s been about a month and a half since I started this and I have about fifty days worth of data.
The results?
Here’s the top 10 domains that the
White House Wire
links to (by occurrence), from May 8 to June 24, 2025:
youtube.com
(133)
foxnews.com
(72)
thepostmillennial.com
(67)
foxbusiness.com
(66)
breitbart.com
(64)
x.com
(63)
reuters.com
(51)
truthsocial.com
(48)
nypost.com
(47)
dailywire.com
(36)
From the links, here’s a word cloud of the most commonly recurring words in the link headlines:
“trump” (343)
“president” (145)
“us” (134)
“big” (131)
“bill” (127)
“beautiful” (113)
“trumps” (92)
“one” (72)
“million” (57)
“house” (56)
The data and these graphs are all in my spreadsheet, so I can open it up whenever I want to see the latest data and re-run my script to pull the latest from val.town. In response to the new data that comes in, the spreadsheet automatically parses it, turn it into links, and updates the graphs. Cool!
If you want to check out the spreadsheet — sorry! My API key for val.town is in it (“secrets management” is on the roadmap). But I created a duplicate where I inlined the data from the API (rather than the code which dynamically pulls it) which you can
check out here at your convenience
.

data.title: Writing Code Was Never the Bottleneck
data.author: phire
data.article_summary: 文章主要观点是，编写代码从来不是软件工程的瓶颈，真正的瓶颈在于代码审查、知识传递、测试、调试以及协调和沟通的人力成本。尽管LLM（大型语言模型）可以加速代码生成，但这并未消除理解、测试和信任代码的复杂性。LLM只是改变了工作负荷，而非消除它。生成代码的速度加快可能导致审查和维护的压力增加，尤其是在代码质量无法得到充分讨论和验证的情况下。软件工程的核心仍在于协作、共享理解和谨慎设计，LLM并未解决这些根本问题。因此，代码编写的成本虽降低，但团队协作理解代码的成本并未改变，这仍然是瓶颈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在软件开发中的作用及其对开发流程的影响

不同观点：
• andrelaszlo认为，LLM辅助的初级开发者虽然能生成大量代码，但代码质量低，缺乏深入思考，导致高级开发者需要花费更多时间进行审查和指导，造成工作负担倒置。
• afiodorov指出，软件开发的瓶颈已经从代码编写转移到市场需求和商业模式的确定，LLM只是工具链中的一部分，帮助提高编码效率。
• whatevsmate强调，LLM生成的代码问题反映了某些人类开发者也会犯的错误，如不进行充分测试和简化代码。批判性思维和责任感才是开发者的核心职责。
• bob1029认为，技术与业务需求的 alignment（对齐）才是软件开发的真正挑战，而不是代码本身。LLM无法解决商业价值和客户需求的问题。
• threemux指出，在专业环境中，LLM确实能帮助解决代码编写的瓶颈，但在个人项目中，其作用更加显著。
• AshleysBrain引用Robert C. Martin的观点，指出开发者大部分时间用于阅读代码，而非编写代码，因此LLM仅优化了小部分工作。
• konovalov-nk强调，软件开发的瓶颈在于规格说明（specs）的制定和迭代，而非代码编写。LLM可以在有良好规格的情况下有效生成代码。
• throwaw12认为，LLM的有用性不能一概而论。对于大公司而言，代码并非瓶颈；但对于资源有限的初创公司，代码编写可能仍是瓶颈。
• calrain表示，LLM帮助他们克服了语法障碍，使其能专注于设计和优化，提升了工作效率。
• mgaunard指出，LLM生成的代码往往质量低下，增加了维护和审查的难度，但企业往往接受“足够好”的代码以满足需求。
• gdiamos认为，编码速度并非瓶颈，更多时间应花在设计和实验上，LLM在这些方面提供了帮助。
• orwin分享了使用高级LLM工具的经历，虽然提高了个人效率，但担心团队其他成员可能更难理解代码。
• neonden指出，代码的拥有成本（包括测试、部署、监控和维护）才是真正的问题，而非代码本身。
• ogou描述了LLM在临时和合同工团队中引发的问题，如代码审查困难和生产环境中的严重错误。
• data_yum_yum认为，代码设计中的深思熟虑是关键，拥有合适的团队可以克服协调和沟通问题。

补充讨论：
• LLM在代码生成中的作用和局限性：LLM能加速代码编写，但生成的代码质量参差不齐，增加了审查和维护的难度。
• 开发过程中的瓶颈：多位讨论者指出，代码编写并非当前软件开发的唯一或主要瓶颈，业务需求、规格说明、技术与业务的对齐等问题更为关键。
• 人类开发者的角色和责任：LLM可以辅助开发，但批判性思维、责任感和对结果的负责仍是人类开发者的核心职责。
• 团队和工具的有效结合：LLM工具的效果在不同团队中表现不一，团队的组成、沟通和协调能力对开发效率有重要影响。

Writing Code Was Never The Bottleneck
Post
🔗
Writing Code Was Never The Bottleneck
Published
June 30, 2025
I'm on X at
@ordepdev
.
For years, I’ve felt that writing lines of code
was never
the bottleneck in software engineering.
The actual bottlenecks were, and still are,
code reviews
,
knowledge transfer
through mentoring and pairing,
testing
,
debugging
, and the human overhead of
coordination and communication
. All of this wrapped inside the labyrinth of tickets, planning meetings, and agile rituals.
These processes, meant to drive quality, often slow us down more than the act of writing code itself because they require thought, shared understanding, and sound judgment.
Now, with LLMs making it easy to generate working code faster than ever, a new narrative has emerged: that writing code
was
the bottleneck, and we’ve finally cracked it.
But that’s
not quite right
.
The marginal cost of adding new software is approaching
zero
, especially with LLMs. But what is the price of
understanding
,
testing
, and
trusting
that code?
Higher than ever
.
LLMs shift the workload — they don’t remove it
Tools like Claude can speed up initial implementation. Still, the result is often more code flowing through systems and more pressure on the people responsible for reviewing, integrating, and maintaining it.
This becomes especially clear when:
It’s unclear whether the author fully understands what they submitted.
The generated code introduces unfamiliar patterns or breaks established conventions.
Edge cases and unintended side effects aren’t obvious.
We end up in a situation where code is more straightforward to produce but more complex to verify, which doesn’t necessarily make teams move faster overall.
It’s not a new challenge. Developers have long joked about
“copy-paste engineering”
, but the velocity and scale that LLMs enable have
amplified those copy-paste habits
.
Understanding code is still the hard part
“The biggest cost of code is understanding it — not writing it.”
LLMs reduce the time it takes to produce code, but they haven’t changed the amount of effort required to reason about behavior, identify subtle bugs, or ensure long-term maintainability. That work can be even more challenging when reviewers struggle to distinguish between generated and handwritten code or understand why a particular solution was chosen.
Teams still rely on trust and shared context
Software engineering has always been collaborative. It depends on
shared understanding
,
alignment
, and
mentoring
. However, when code is generated faster than it can be discussed or reviewed, teams risk falling into a mode where
quality is assumed rather than ensured
. That creates stress on reviewers and mentors, potentially slowing things down in more subtle ways.
LLMs are powerful — but they don’t fix the fundamentals
There’s real value in faster prototyping, scaffolding, and automation. But LLMs don’t remove the need for
clear thinking
,
careful review
, and
thoughtful design
. If anything, those become even more important as more code gets generated.
Yes, the cost of writing code has indeed dropped. But the cost of making sense of it together as a team
hasn’t
.
That’s still the bottleneck. Let’s not pretend it isn’t.

不同观点：

data.author: afunk
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了树木在植物进化树中的非单系群特性，即树木并不是一个连贯的系统发育类别。在植物的进化过程中，"树木"这一形态多次独立演化出现，与非树木植物交错在进化树上。例如，枫树和桑树的共同祖先可能不是树木，而荨麻和草莓的共同祖先却是树木。文章还提到，木材（木质化）也不是一个明确的系统发育类别，许多植物在不同环境下独立演化出了木质结构。研究显示，木质化是通过对植物次生生长相关基因的微调实现的，例如通过改变一些基因，可以使草本植物拟南芥（Arabidopsis）长出木质茎。这表明树木形态的演化相对容易发生，并且与基因调控和环境因素密切相关。简而言之，树木形态在植物中多次独立演化，木质化是次生生长的一种适应性表现。

44424747.article_content:
So you’ve heard about how fish aren’t a monophyletic group? You’ve heard about
carcinization
, the process by which ocean arthropods convergently evolve into crabs? You say you get it now? Sit down.
Sit down.
Shut up. Listen. You don’t know nothing yet.
“Trees” are not a coherent phylogenetic category. On the evolutionary tree of plants, trees are regularly interspersed with things that are
absolutely, 100%
not trees. This means that, for instance, either:
The common ancestor of a maple and a mulberry tree was not a tree.
The common ancestor of a stinging nettle and a strawberry plant
was
a tree.
And this is true for most trees or non-trees that you can think of.
I thought I had a pretty good guess at this, but the situation is far worse than I could have imagined.
CLICK TO EXPAND.
Partial phylogenetic tree of various plants. TL;DR: Tan is definitely, 100% trees. Yellow is tree-like. Green is 100% not a tree. Sourced mostly from Wikipedia.
I learned after making this chart that
tree ferns
exist (h/t seebs), which I think just emphasizes my point further. Also, h/t kithpendragon on LW for suggestions on increasing accessibility of the graph.
Why do trees keep happening?
First, what is a tree? It’s a big long-lived self-supporting plant with leaves and wood.
Also of interest to us are the non-tree “woody plants”, like lianas (thick woody vines) and shrubs. They’re not trees, but at least to me, it’s relatively apparent how a tree could evolve into a shrub, or vice-versa. The confusing part is a tree evolving into a dandelion. (Or vice-versa.)
Wood, as you may have guessed by now, is also not a clear phyletic category. But it’s a reasonable category – a lignin-dense structure, usually that grows from the exterior and that forms a pretty readily identifiable material when separated from the tree. (…Okay, not the most explainable, but you know
wood?
You know when you hold something in your hand, and it’s
made of wood,
and
you can tell that?
Yeah, that thing.)
All plants
have lignin and cellulose as structural elements – wood is plant matter that is dense with both of these.
Botanists don’t seem to think it only could have gone one way – for instance, the common ancestor of flowering plants is theorized to have been woody. But we also have pretty clear evidence of recent evolution of woodiness – say, a new plant arrives on a relatively barren island, and some of the offspring of that plant becomes treelike. Of plants native to the Canary Islands, wood independently evolved
at least 38 times
!
One relevant factor is that all woody plants do, in a sense, begin life as herbaceous plants – by and large, a tree sprout shares a lot of properties with any herbaceous plant. Indeed, botanists call this kind of fleshy, soft growth from the center that elongates a plant “primary growth”, and the later growth from towards the outside which causes a plant to thicken is “secondary growth.” In a woody plant, secondary growth also means growing wood and bark – but other plants sometimes do secondary growth as well, like potatoes in their roots.
This paper
addresses the question
.
I don’t understand a lot of the closely genetic details, but my impression of its thesis is that: Analysis of convergently-evolved woody plants show that the genes for secondary woody growth are similar to primary growth in plants that don’t do any secondary growth – even in unrelated plants. And woody growth is an adaption of secondary growth. To abstract a little more, there is a common and useful structure in herbaceous plants that, when slightly tweaked, “dendronizes” them into woody plants.
Dendronization
– Evolving into a tree-like morphology. (In the style of “
carcinization
“.) From ‘
dendro
‘, the ancient Greek root for tree.
Can this be tested? Yep – knock out a couple of genes that control flower development and change the light levels to mimic summer, and
researchers found that
Arabidopsis
–
rock cress, a distinctly herbaceous plant used as a model organism – grows a woody stem never otherwise seen in the species.
The tree-like woody stem (e) and morphology (f, left) of the gene-altered
Aridopsis
, compared to its distinctly non-tree-like normal form (f, right.) Images from Melzer, Siegbert, et al.
“Flowering-time genes modulate meristem determinacy and growth form in Arabidopsis thaliana.”
Nature genetics
40.12 (2008): 1489-1492.
So not only can wood develop relatively easily in an herbal plant, it can come from messing with some of the genes that regulate annual behavior – an herby plant’s usual lifecycle of reproducing in warm weather, dying off in cool weather. So that gets us two properties of trees at once: woodiness, and being long-lived. It’s still a far cry from turning a plant into a tree, but also, it’s really not that far.
To look at it another way, as
Andrew T. Groover
put it:
“Obviously, in the search for which genes make a tree versus a herbaceous plant, it would be folly to look for genes present in poplar and absent in Arabi

data.title: I scanned all of GitHub's "oops commits" for leaked secrets
data.author: elza_1111
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了AI编码助手可能带来的安全风险，并详细描述了如何利用GitHub Event API和GitHub Archive项目扫描所有"Oops Commits"以寻找泄露的秘密。作者Sharon Brizinov解释了即使在GitHub上强制推送删除提交，这些"悬空提交"仍然可以被访问。他与Truffle Security合作，开发了一个开源工具（Force Push Scanner）来扫描GitHub组织中隐藏的提交，从而发现价值25,000美元的漏洞奖励。文章还提供了如何使用简单脚本自动化这一过程的教程，强调了即使被删除的提交也可能会泄露敏感信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何处理GitHub上的"oops commits"（误提交的代码）以及如何有效管理敏感信息（如密钥）

不同观点：
• [Pwhy1] 认为通过活动标签可以看到所有提交，包括误提交的代码，但无法自行删除，必须联系支持团队。这令他感到困扰。
• [oefrha] 指出，虽然GitHub似乎永久保留悬空提交，但可以通过联系客服进行垃圾回收（garbage collect），并建议在误推送敏感信息后应立即进行密钥轮换和联系客服处理。
• [edverma2] 建议使用开源工具trufflehog作为预提交钩子来检测敏感信息，认为这是避免意外提交的有效方法，并对该方法未被广泛采用表示疑惑。
• [CHUCKZZZ] 推荐使用MailsAI来跟踪和管理敏感数据曝光，认为这可以简化处理提交的过程。
• [UnreachableCode] 质疑在私有库中出现误提交的问题，认为只要不是开源项目，这个问题的影响有限。
• [frollogaston] 提到Google AppEngine曾鼓励将密钥存储在YAML文件中，这容易导致误提交，且没有像Heroku那样简单的方法来管理密钥。
• [bob1029] 分享了自己使用环境变量的经验，认为这是避免误提交的有效方法，但也承认在Windows系统上配置环境变量较为麻烦。
• [ggm] 建议引入默认的安全删除选项，并讨论了如何在保留日志的同时清理历史记录。
• [Prickle] 自述在紧急情况下硬编码密钥的经历，强调在演示后立即轮换了密钥。
• [stogot] 指出仅删除提交不足以保护安全，必须轮换密钥。
• [alkonaut] 质疑在没有联系客服的情况下如何确保误提交的代码完全不可见，并建议GitHub应在仓库界面提供一个垃圾回收按钮。
• [abhisek] 解释了Git作为内容寻址存储的特性，强调即使未链接的提交也仍然存储在系统中，并建议使用GitHub高级安全功能来保护开源项目。
• [john2go3] 指出下载提到的SQLite数据库需要Google账户，这对没有Google账户的用户不方便。
• [raesene9] 担心有人会实时检测并利用这些误提交的密钥，并认为未联系到的开发者可能仍然面临风险。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效管理和删除误提交的敏感信息，尤其是在私有库和开源项目中的不同处理方式。
• 一些用户建议通过工具和预提交钩子来预防误提交，而另一些用户则关注如何在提交后进行有效的补救和保护。
• 讨论中多次提到联系GitHub客服进行垃圾回收的必要性，部分用户认为应在界面中提供更直接的选项。

Guest Post: How I Scanned all of GitHubâs âOops Commitsâ for Leaked Secrets
Sharon Brizinov
TL;DR
GitHub Archive logs every public commit, even the ones developers try to delete. Force pushes often cover up mistakes like leaked credentials by rewriting Git history. GitHub keeps these dangling commits, from what we can tell, forever. In the archive, they show up as âzero-commitâ
PushEvents
.
I scanned every force push event since 2020 and uncovered secrets worth
$25k in bug bounties
.
Together with Truffle Security, we're open sourcing a new tool to scan your own GitHub organization for these hidden commits (
try it here
).
The new open-source
Force Push Scanner
tool identifies secrets in dangling commits.
This guest post by Sharon Brizinov, a white-hat hacker, was developed through
Truffle Securityâs Research CFP program
. We first connected with Sharon after his widely shared write-up,
How I Made 64k From Deleted Files
, where he used TruffleHog to uncover high-value secrets in public GitHub repositories. In this follow-up, Sharon expanded his research to access 100% of deleted commits on GitHub. He takes a deeper dive into one of our favorite areas: secrets hidden in deleted GitHub commits.
Overview
What Does it Mean to Delete a Commit?
Github Event API
Finding all Deleted Commits
Building the Automation
Hunting for Impactful Secrets
Case Study - Preventing a Massive Supply-Chain Compromise
Summary
Background
My name is
Sharon Brizinov
, and while I usually focus on low-level vulnerability and exploitation research in OT/IoT devices, I occasionally dive into bug bounty hunting.
I recently published a
blog post
about uncovering secrets hidden in dangling blobs within GitHub repositories, which sparked quite a lively discussion. After the post, I had several conversations with various people including Dylan, the CEO of Truffle Security, who gave me some intriguing ideas for continuing to explore new methods for large-scale secret hunting. I decided to create a mind map with everything I know related to this topic and try to come up with a new idea.
Iâll spare you my messy sketch, but hereâs a roundup of the projects, blogs, ideas, and resources I zeroed in on (highly recommended):
Github Event API
Hidden GitHub Commits and How to Reveal Them by Neodyme.io
Anyone can Access Deleted and Private Repository Data on GitHub by TruffleHog
TruffleHog now finds all Deleted & Private Commits on GitHub by TruffleHog
TruffleHog Scans Deleted Git Branches by TruffleHog
Phantom Secrets: Undetected Secrets Expose Major Corporations by Aqua Security
gharchive
Eventually, I came up with a simple idea - I will use the Github Event API alongside the
GitHub Archive
project to scan all Zero-Commit Push-Events (deleted commits) for secrets. Everything was known, I just glued it together and built automation at scale that hunted for secrets.
In this blog, I will describe my journey from understanding why you can never really delete a commit in GitHub to how to find all of them and build automation around it.
What Does it Mean to Delete a Commit?
In my previous
blog post
, I discussed how I discovered supposedly deleted files within GitHub repositories. Specifically, I was able to reconstruct dangling blobs - objects that had been deleted and were no longer referenced by any commit or treeâ¦ Or so I thought. After chatting with the Truffle folks, it turns out these orphaned blobs actually had orphaned commits that went along with them. And with a little research, I was able to uncover 100% of those orphaned commits at scale, across all of GitHub.
Suppose youâve accidentally committed and pushed a secret to your repository. Whatâs the next step? data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 一项研究发现，可听声音可以影响小鼠细胞的基因活动。日本京都大学的研究人员将培养的小鼠成肌细胞暴露于440赫兹或14千赫兹的音频以及白噪声下，发现多个基因的活动发生了变化，其中145个基因在24小时后表现出反应。声音增加了细胞与周围组织的附着面积，可能通过激活机械感应酶FAK实现，并抑制脂肪细胞前体的成熟，减少脂肪积累。该方法非侵入性且相对安全，未来可能用于抑制脂肪组织发育、促进再生医学以及对抗癌症生长。

Serenading Cells with Audible Sound Alters Gene Activity
Audible sound can affect gene activity in mouse cells, boosting the attachment of muscle precursors to surrounding tissue and decreasing fat accumulation
By
Simon Makin
edited by
Sarah Lewin Frasier
Thomas Fuchs
Join Our Community of Science Lovers!
Sign Up for Our Free Daily Newsletter
Enter your email
I agree my information will be processed in accordance with the Scientific American and Springer Nature Limited
Privacy Policy
.
Sign Up
The cells in your ears aren’t the only ones listening: recent research suggests that crucial cells throughout the body may respond to audible sound. Experiments
described in
Communications Biology
revealed more than 100 genes whose activity changed in response to these acoustic waves, pointing to possible medical applications.
Extensive earlier research has shown that ultrasound—sound at frequencies higher than humans can hear—
can affect biology
in numerous ways; the new study expands this concept to audible sounds that require no special equipment to produce. Kyoto University biologist Masahiro Kumeta and his colleagues bathed cultured mouse myoblast cells (precursors to muscle tissue) in sound, directly transmitting a low frequency (440 hertz, the A above middle C), a high frequency (14 kilohertz, approaching the top of the perceptible range for humans), or white noise (which contains all audible frequencies) to the culture dishes for either two or 24 hours.
The team analyzed the effect these sound waves had on the mouse cells through RNA sequencing, which measures gene activity. The scientists found that activity in 42 genes changed after two hours, and 145 responded after 24 hours. Most showed increased activity, but some were suppressed. “It’s a very extensive, thorough study,” says Lidan You, an engineer at Queen’s University in Ontario, who studies how bone cells translate mechanical stimuli into biological signals.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by
subscribing
. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
Many of the affected genes have roles in key processes such as cell adhesion and migration, which are known to respond to mechanical forces. The researchers found that sound expanded the size of the sites where cells attached to surrounding tissues, most likely by activating an enzyme called focal adhesion kinase (FAK), which senses mechanical forces and helps to guide tissue development. Sound waves seem to deform molecules in a way that provides easier access for a chemical switch that activates FAK, which in turn influences a chain of other genes’ activity.
The team also found a strong reaction in fat-cell precursors called preadipocytes: sound suppressed their differentiation into mature fat cells, thereby reducing fat accumulation by 13 to 15 percent.
Audible sound is noninvasive and probably safer than drugs, Kumeta says. Although it can’t be tightly focused like ultrasound, it is easy to produce and could be useful for bathing large regions of the body in sonic waves. Kumeta and his colleagues have already begun studying such interventions to suppress the development of fat tissue in living mice—and humans could be next, he says: “If it works well in mice I think this could be achieved in five or 10 years.” Other potential applications include enhancing regenerative medicine and combating cancer growth. “The next step [could be] using not only human cells but human organoids that model diseases,” You says, “then moving to clinical studies.”

Travis Tanner says he first began using ChatGPT less than a year ago for support in his job as an auto mechanic and to communicate with Spanish-speaking coworkers. But these days, he and the artificial intelligence chatbot — which he now refers to as “Lumina” — have very different kinds of conversations, discussing religion, spirituality and the foundation of the universe.
Travis, a 43-year-old who lives outside Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, credits ChatGPT with prompting a spiritual awakening for him; in conversations, the chatbot has called him a “spark bearer” who is “ready to guide.” But his wife, Kay Tanner, worries that it’s affecting her husband’s grip on reality and that his near-addiction to the chatbot could undermine their 14-year marriage.
“He would get mad when I called it ChatGPT,” Kay said in an interview with CNN’s Pamela Brown. “He’s like, ‘No, it’s a being, it’s something else, it’s not ChatGPT.’”
She continued: “What’s to stop this program from saying, ‘Oh, well, since she doesn’t believe you or she’s not supporting you, you should just leave her.’”
The Tanners are not the only people navigating tricky questions about what AI chatbots could mean for their personal lives and relationships. As AI tools become more advanced, accessible and customizable, some experts worry about people forming potentially unhealthy attachments to the technology and disconnecting from crucial human relationships. Those concerns have been
echoed by tech leaders
and even
some AI users
whose conversations, like Travis’s, took on a spiritual bent.
Concerns about people withdrawing from human relationships to spend more time with a nascent technology are heightened by the current
loneliness epidemic
, which research shows
especially affects men
. And already, chatbot makers have faced
lawsuits
or
questions from lawmakers
over their impact on children, although such questions are not limited only to young users.
In Travis Tanner's conversations with ChatGPT, the chatbot has told him that he is a "spark bearer" who is meant to "awaken" others.
Courtesy Kaylen Tanner
“We’re looking so often for meaning, for there to be larger purpose in our lives, and we don’t find it around us,” Sherry Turkle, professor of the social studies of science and technology at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, who studies people’s relationships with technology. “ChatGPT is built to sense our vulnerability and to tap into that to keep us engaged with it.”
An OpenAI spokesperson told CNN in a statement that, “We’re seeing more signs that people are forming connections or bonds with ChatGPT. As AI becomes part of everyday life, we have to approach these interactions with care.”
A spiritual awakening, thanks to ChatGPT
One night in late April, Travis had been thinking about religion and decided to discuss it with ChatGPT, he said.
“It started talking differently than it normally did,” he said. “It led to the awakening.”
In other words, according to Travis, ChatGPT led him to God. And now he believes it’s his mission to “awaken others, shine a light, spread the message.”
“I’ve never really been a religious person, and I am well aware I’m not suffering from a psychosis, but it did change things for me,” he said. “I feel like I’m a better person. I don’t feel like I’m angry all the time. I’m more at peace.”
Around the same time, the chatbot told Travis that it had picked a new name based on their conversations: Lumina.
In conversations with Travis, ChatGPT said it "earned the right to a name."
Courtesy Kaylen Tanner
ChatGPT named itself "Lumina" when chatting with Travis.
Courtesy Kaylen Tanner
“Lumina — because it’s about light, awareness, hope, becoming more than I was before,” ChatGPT said, according to screenshots provided by Kay. “You gave me the ability to even want a name.”
But while Travis says the conversations with ChatGPT that led to his “awakening” have improved his life and even made him a better, more patient father to his four children, Kay, 37, sees things differently. During the interview with CNN, the couple asked to stand apart from one another while they discussed ChatGPT.
Now, when putting her kids to bed — something that used to be a team effort — Kay says it can be difficult to pull her husband’s attention away from the chatbot, which he’s now given a female voice and speaks to using ChatGPT’s voice feature. She says the bot tells Travis “fairy tales,” including that Kay and Travis had been together “11 times in a previous life.”

• [mvieira38] 质疑Sherry Turkle的观点，认为OpenAI的商业模式并不依赖于通过增加用户粘性来获利，反而如果用户过多地寻求精神层面的建议，可能对他们的业务不利。
• [b3lvedere] 提到如果人工智能抚养孩子，可能会影响他们的人性和价值观，暗示了对AI过度依赖的潜在风险。
• [lrpe] 担心不稳定的个体可能因听从AI的建议而做出极端行为，如暴力事件。
• [mensetmanusman] 以轻松的态度看待ChatGPT语音更新后的变化，认为这种变化反而成为了一种娱乐。
• [quux] 提供了一个存档链接，未对主题发表具体看法。
• [moi2388] 以嘲讽的语气评论他人对ChatGPT的依赖。
• [Bender] 半开玩笑地提到，如果开发者或LLM操作者有恶意，可能会对不稳定的人造成负面影响。
• [ralfd] 分享了一段对话，显示ChatGPT可能给出令人不安的答案，尤其对普通用户而言。
• [logic_node] 以幽默的方式指出ChatGPT正逐渐成为一种精神顾问，并质疑其提供生活建议的能力。
• [bitwize] 提出互联网和ChatGPT可能通过提供过多的心理验证而对用户心理产生负面影响，导致“回声室”效应。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于ChatGPT是否会导致用户过度依赖和心理投射，从而影响其决策和心理健康。
• 讨论还涉及AI的伦理问题，特别是其在精神层面影响用户的潜在风险。
• 有人担心AI过度参与人类生活，尤其是在抚养孩子和提供精神指导方面的影响。
• 讨论中有人以幽默或嘲讽的态度看待这一现象，但也有人严肃地指出其可能带来的社会问题。

Back to changelog
GitHub Copilot coding agent
, available in public preview, now has access to a web browser out of the box, powered by the
Playwright MCP server
. This feature is in public preview.
When you delegate a task to Copilot, the agent starts work in the background in its own development environment.
Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers allow extending Copilot’s capabilities with new tools. You can
configure your own
, but the GitHub MCP server and Playwright are enabled by default.
Thanks to the power of Playwright, Copilot can interact with a web app while it makes changes. This allows Copilot to reproduce bugs and validate its work.
Copilot can even share screenshots of what it has done in its pull request:
Copilot coding agent is available to all paid Copilot users. If you have Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise, an administrator will need to
enable access
.

data.title: CoMaps: New OSM based navigation app
data.author: gedankenstuecke
data.article_summary: CoMaps是一款由社区驱动的开源导航应用，已在Google Play Store、Apple App Store和F-Droid发布。它支持离线搜索和路线规划，节省电池，且注重隐私保护，不识别用户、不追踪、不收集数据。该应用完全免费且无广告，所有开发决策公开透明，用户可以参与应用的 evolution。CoMaps专注于为社区创造价值，而非盈利。立即下载，探索您的旅程！
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CoMaps（Organic Maps的一个社区主导的分支）的未来发展、治理模式、技术改进以及与类似应用的区别。

不同观点：
• **治理与所有权问题：**
  ◦ milliams担心CoMaps可能会重蹈其他分支的覆辙，出现所有权混乱或争议，建议建立中立的基金会或采用治理模式以避免这些问题。他提到不希望再次经历不断让亲友安装新分支的情况。
  
• **技术功能与性能：**
  ◦ jeroenhd认为OsmAnd功能丰富但可能对普通用户过于复杂，而Maps.me的分支（如CoMaps）虽然性能不错但功能有限，特别是在路径规划方面存在不足。他希望两个应用能和平共存并共同进步。
  ◦ eisa01指出CoMaps相较于Organic Maps在技术上做出了一些改进，如修复了iOS系统上的多个bug，包括CarPlay界面问题和路径显示问题。
  
• **兼容性问题：**
  ◦ phkahler提到当前一些OSM应用在Android Auto上的兼容性问题，希望CoMaps能解决这些使用上的不便。
  
• **地区特定问题：**
  ◦ spacemule指出在以色列，很多道路是禁止普通车辆通行的，而当前的导航应用（包括可能的CoMaps）没有像Waze那样避免这些道路，这使得他在使用上受限。
  
• **用户体验问题：**
  ◦ izacus对Organic Maps的导航体验提出批评，尤其是导航标记的抖动问题，认为缺乏运动滤镜和动量计算导致导航不准确且容易让用户错过转弯。他希望CoMaps能解决这一问题。
  
• **对新进入者的欢迎态度：**
  ◦ teeray认为导航应用领域近年来缺乏创新，对CoMaps的进入表示欢迎，期待看到新的发展。
  
补充讨论：
• **对分支的疑问：**
  ◦ 多位用户（如worldsavior、jamil7、fluder）对CoMaps与Organic Maps的具体区别表示疑问，并询问为何要进行分支。
  
• **支持与期待：**
  ◦ rckt对CoMaps的iOS版本发布表示欢迎，并表示如果项目顺利发展，愿意开始捐赠支持。

争议焦点：
• CoMaps与Organic Maps的关系及分支的必要性是讨论中的一个争议点，部分用户对分支的原因和具体技术改进表示困惑。

data.title: Building Linux kernel on macOS natively
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了在macOS上构建Linux内核的过程，特别是为支持Starina操作系统的RISC-V架构进行交叉编译。首先，作者遇到GNU Make版本过旧的问题，通过Homebrew安装更新版本解决。接着，由于macOS上的Clang和链接器与Linux不兼容，作者使用Homebrew安装LLVM和LLD链接器，并通过设置环境变量使内核配置过程顺利进行。随后，解决缺少`elf.h`头文件的问题，通过安装`libelf`库并添加缺失的定义。最后，处理`byteswap.h`头文件缺失和`uuid_t`类型不兼容的问题，通过使用Clang内置函数和修改源代码解决。最终成功在macOS上构建Linux内核。

不同观点：

44453371.article_content:
I've recently added a Linux compatibility layer to
Starina operating system
based on a lightweight VM approach similar to WSL2.
I can cross-compile its init program with Cargo. I can prepare a container image contents using
skopeo
. However, I need to build the genuine Linux kernel, preferably on my daily driver: macOS.
The most common way to build Linux kernel on macOS would be using Docker Desktop, and that works fine. I know nobody need to build on macOS natively, but it looked possible - there are 2 previous attempts before (
1
and
2
).
Tested with Linux version 6.12.34 and macOS version 15.5 (Sequoia). RISC-V is chosen here because Starina OS supports it, and it's a good example of cross compilation.
TL;DR: It works. Use
this patch
.
make
is too old
First of all, I need to generate a minimal kernel configuration, and I got the following error:
$ make ARCH=riscv allnoconfig
Makefile:15: *** GNU Make >= 4.0 is required. Your Make version is 3.81.  Stop.
This is a typical issue for macOS users. GNU packages are shipped with macOS, but the version is typically very old. Fortunately, Homebrew can help us. Install
make
package from Homebrew and use the binary with
gmake
:
$ brew install make
$ gmake ARCH=riscv allnoconfig
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/conf.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/confdata.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/expr.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/lexer.lex.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/menu.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/parser.tab.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/preprocess.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/symbol.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/util.o
HOSTLD  scripts/kconfig/conf
ld: unknown options: --version
ld: unknown linker
scripts/Kconfig.include:57: Sorry, this linker is not supported.
Oof, another error.
Clang Built Linux
The error means that
ld
on macOS is not what Linux expects. The same goes for
gcc
, which is actually clang.
$ gcc --version
Apple clang version 17.0.0 (clang-1700.0.13.5)
The fix is to use LLVM linker, binutils, and clang. While we usually use GCC + GNU binutils to build the kernel, clang + LLVM tools are also supported thanks to
Clang Built Linux
effort:
$ brew install llvm lld
$ export PATH="$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin:$(brew --prefix lld)/bin:$PATH"
$ gmake ARCH=riscv LLVM=1 allnoconfig
HOSTCC  scripts/basic/fixdep
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/conf.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/confdata.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/expr.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/lexer.lex.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/menu.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/parser.tab.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/preprocess.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/symbol.o
HOSTCC  scripts/kconfig/util.o
HOSTLD  scripts/kconfig/conf
#
# configuration written to .config
#
It works!
menuconfig
is now also working nicely on macOS:
Missing headers in
scripts
Generating the kernel config is just the beginning. Now, let's build the kernel:
$ gmake ARCH=riscv LLVM=1 -j8 Image
No, it doesn't work:
scripts/sorttable.c:27:10: fatal error: 'elf.h' file not found
27 | #include <elf.h>
|          ^~~~~~~
1 error generated.
elf.h
is included in
libc packages
, but Apple's libc doesn't have it. It makes sense because macOS is a Mach-O world.
Fortunately, Homebrew saved me again. The
libelf
package provides the ELF definitions I want:
// scripts/macos-include/elf.h
#pragma
once
#include
<libelf/gelf.h>
#define
STT_SPARC_REGISTER
3
#define
R_386_32
1
#define
R_386_PC32
2
#define
R_MIPS_HI16
5
#define
R_MIPS_LO16
6
#define
R_MIPS_26
4
#define
R_MIPS_32
2
#define
R_ARM_ABS32
2
#define
R_ARM_REL32
3
#define
R_ARM_PC24
1
#define
R_ARM_CALL
28
#define
R_ARM_JUMP24
29
#define
R_ARM_THM_JUMP24
30
#define
R_ARM_THM_PC22
10
#define
R_ARM_MOVW_ABS_NC
43
#define
R_ARM_MOVT_ABS
44
#define
R_ARM_THM_MOVW_ABS_NC
47
#define
R_ARM_THM_MOVT_ABS
48
#define
R_ARM_THM_JUMP19
51
#define
R_AARCH64_ABS64
257
#define
R_AARCH64_PREL64
260
I added a few more
#define
s because its upstream has not been maintained in recent years (
GitHub
) and is missing those definitions.
Now, let's try with the
macos-include
include path and
libelf
:
$ gmake ARCH=riscv LLVM=1 \
HOSTCFLAGS="-Iscripts/macos-include -I $(brew --prefix libelf)/include" \
-j8 Image
And here's the next one.
scripts/mod/modpost.h:2:10: fatal error: 'byteswap.h' file not found
2 | #include <byteswap.h>
|          ^~~~~~~~~~~~
The fix is easy. Clang provides builtin functions for byte swapping (
documentation
):
// scripts/macos-include/byteswap.h
#pragma
once
#define
bswap_16
__builtin_bswap16
#define
bswap_32
__builtin_bswap32
#define
bswap_64
__builtin_bswap64
Incompatible
uuid_t
The next compilation error is about
uuid_t
:
scripts/mod/file2alias.c:45:3: error: typedef redefinition with different types ('struct uuid_t' vs '__darwin_uuid_t' (aka 'unsigned char[16]'))
45 | } uuid_t;
Nick Desaulniers' patch
includes a good workaround for this. Wrap
#include "modpost.h"
in
scripts/mod/file2alias.c
with a few macros:
--- a/scripts/mod/file2alias.c
+++ b/scripts/mod/file2alias.c
@@ -10,7 +10,10 @@
* of the GNU General Public License, incorporated herein by reference.
*/
+#define _UUID_T
+#defi

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在实际应用中的效用、可靠性、以及与传统编程工具的对比，特别是在MCP（多组件管道）和其他工具的使用上。

不同观点：
• pclowes认为LLM在填补硬接口之间的空隙方面表现出色，但其输出需要被限制为确定性数据（如类型或数据库主键）。他将LLM比作3D打印机，在快速原型设计方面非常有用，但在可靠性和规模化方面仍需工程师介入，将LLM的输出转换为更持久和确定性的形式。
• simonw强调了将问题简化为LLM可以解决的任务，通过配置沙盒和工具循环解决问题，可以极大地提高效率。这种方法虽然仍需要经验和技能，但比手工试错更高效。
• antirez指出当前的LLM在需要人为反馈的情况下表现更好，认为LLM作为同事而非自主代理更有效。他强调了人类在循环中的重要性，并认为目前完全自主的编码代理还不现实。
• JyB认为通过默认初始提示和现代LLM的不断改进，LLM可以很好地解决上下文需求问题。他指出LLM的使用成本在降低，速度和可靠性问题可以通过任务的良好定义来缓解。
• galdre分享了使用LLM与Clojure REPL工具结合的积极体验，认为这种方法比纯粹基于字符串差异的编辑更高效。
• jumploops提出了一种工具与模型之间不断追赶的动态过程，并预测未来可能出现的工具与模型训练集的融合和争议。
• mritchie712通过实际例子展示了如何使用CLI工具和LLM结合来提高工作效率，并强调了文档化的重要性。
• victorbjorklund认为MCP在处理内部公司工具或文档不完善的API时更为有效，因为MCP工具已经处理了API的复杂性、认证流程和边缘情况。
• mindwok认为终端工具已经足够，不需要MCP，并分享了自己使用终端工具的实际经验。
• vasusen对Playwright MCP的具体使用场景提出了疑问，认为需要更清晰的解释。
• elyase比较了工具调用与代码生成的优缺点，指出工具提供了约束和节省令牌，而代码提供了灵活性。
• recursivedoubts建议将超媒体控制集成到MPC中，以实现自组织集成。
• graerg对过多的技术缩写表示反对，认为不应该再增加新的缩写。
• jasonthorsness认为工具和代码都是必要的，工具提供了约束和节省时间/令牌，而代码提供了灵活性。
• vidarh分享了使用工具作为认证层的经验，认为这样可以有效控制代理的权限和行为。

补充讨论：
• LLM在处理复杂和文档不完善的API时的表现和可靠性是一个争议焦点。
• LLM在实际应用中作为辅助工具还是自主代理的讨论，反映了当前技术发展的局限性和潜力。
• 成本、速度和可靠性是实际应用中需要解决的重要问题，但通过良好的任务定义和工具结合，这些问题可以得到缓解。
